search_subtitle: How do I find a job in Austria?
application_subtitle: How do I apply for a job in Austria
rights_subtitle: Employment contract, wages, working hours and vacation
certification_subtitle: Recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications
entity1.id1.title: Important documents for an application
entity1.id1.subtitle: A complete application usually consists of:
entity1.id1.entry1.title: 1) Cover letter (or letter of motivation)
entity1.id1.entry1.subtitle:
• A short letter (usually 1 page)
• In it you explain:
• Why you are interested in the job
• Why you're a good fit for this
• What you know about the company
• Important: friendly, polite and error-free
• When writing your motivation letter, pay attention to the important points of the job advertisement.Refer to the required points in the letter of motivation (e.g. why YOU meet these qualifications)

Example:
Dear Ms. Müller,
I am applying for the position as a saleswoman because I enjoy contact with people
and I already have experience in customer service.
Kind regards
[Your name]
entity1.id1.entry2.title: 2) Curriculum Vitae (CV)
entity1.id1.entry2.subtitle:
• An overview of your journey so far
• Usually structured in a table
• Contains:
• Personal data (name, address, date of birth, contact)
• Training (school, vocational training, studies)
• Work experience or internships
• Knowledge (e.g. languages, computers)
• Interests or hobbies (optional)
• Date and signature
• Website to customize and write CV for job for free https://
www.livecareer.de/lebenslauf-muster
• The CV can also be graphically adapted to the company.
entity1.id1.entry3.title: 3) Certificates and evidence
entity1.id1.entry3.subtitle:
• School reports
• Employment references or internship confirmations
• Course confirmations or diplomas (e.g. first aid, language course, computer skills)
entity1.id2.title: How do you apply?
entity1.id2.subtitle: This is how you can apply
entity1.id2.entry1.title: 1) By email (attach application documents as PDF)
entity1.id2.entry2.title: 2) Online form (e.g. via a company website)
entity1.id2.entry3.title: 3) By mail (less common)
entity1.id2.entry4.title: 4) Personal (e.g. for smaller companies or shops)
entity1.id2.entry5.title: 5) Job advertisements can be found on AMS.at, enter the desired professional areas in Google (e.g.: salesperson)
entity1.id2.entry7.title:
Tip: Pay attention to the job advertisement - it says exactly what the company requires and how you are
should apply.
entity1.id3.title: job interview
entity1.id3.subtitle: If you are invited
entity1.id3.entry1.title: 1) Prepare yourself
entity1.id3.entry1.subtitle:
• Find out more about the company
• Think about why you want to work there
• Think about what you are good at
entity1.id3.entry2.title: 2) Dress neatly and neatly
entity1.id3.entry3.title: 3) Be punctual and friendly
entity1.id4.title: Further requirements (depending on the job)
entity1.id4.subtitle: If you are invited
entity1.id4.entry1.title: 1) Vocational training or studies (e.g. nursing, crafts, office)
entity1.id4.entry2.title: 2) Language skills
entity1.id4.entry3.title: 3) Valid work permit (if you are not from the EU)
entity1.id4.entry4.title: 4) Driving license (sometimes required)
entity2.id1.title: Employment contracts - basics
entity2.id1.subtitle: What must be in the employment contract?
entity2.id1.entry1.title: Written form
entity2.id1.entry1.subtitle: The employer must submit a written contract no later than one month after the start of work.Oral contracts are also valid, but are more difficult to prove.
entity2.id1.entry2.title: Mandatory information
entity2.id1.entry2.subtitle: Contract must contain: names of the parties, place of work, start date, salary, working hours, vacation entitlement, notice periods.
entity2.id1.entry3.title: Probationary period
entity2.id1.entry3.subtitle: Maximum 1 month trial period.During this time the notice period is 1 week.After the probationary period, statutory notice periods apply.
entity2.id1.entry4.title: Fixed-term contracts
entity2.id1.entry4.subtitle: Fixed-term contracts must be objectively justified (e.g. project work, seasonal work).Possible for a maximum of 4 years, then automatically permanent.
entity2.id2.title: Contract types & special features
entity2.id2.subtitle: Different working relationships
entity2.id2.entry1.title: Full-time vs. part-time
entity2.id2.entry1.subtitle: Full-time: Typically 38.5 hours/week.Part-time: Fewer hours, proportional holiday and salary entitlement.
entity2.id2.entry2.title: Apprenticeship training
entity2.id2.entry2.subtitle: Apprentices have special rights: limited working hours, right to vocational school, apprentice compensation instead of salary.
entity2.id2.entry3.title: Marginal employment
entity2.id2.entry3.subtitle: Up to €485.85 per month (2023).No vacation entitlement, but health insurance.Tax and social security free.
entity2.id2.entry4.title: Contract for work & freelancers
entity2.id2.entry4.subtitle: Not employees, but self-employed people.Fewer rights (no vacation, no protection against dismissal).Beware of false self-employment!
entity2.id3.title: Salary & Wages
entity2.id3.subtitle: Payment rights
entity2.id3.entry1.title: Minimum wage
entity2.id3.entry1.subtitle: No general statutory minimum wage, but collective agreements regulate industry-specific minimum salaries.Without KV, standard market wages apply.
entity2.id3.entry2.title: Payment of wages
entity2.id3.entry2.subtitle: Salary must be paid monthly, on time and in euros.Cash payment only with consent.Received pay slips (payslips).
entity2.id3.entry3.title: overtime
entity2.id3.entry3.subtitle: A maximum of 5 hours of overtime per day, 60 hours per week including overtime.Surcharge of at least 50% or time compensation.
entity2.id3.entry4.title: Night and Sunday work
entity2.id3.entry4.subtitle: Night work (8 p.m.-5 a.m.): Minimum surcharge 50%.Sundays and public holidays: minimum surcharge 100%.Exceptions for certain industries.
entity2.id4.title: Working hours and breaks
entity2.id4.subtitle: Legal boundaries
entity2.id4.entry1.title: Daily working hours
entity2.id4.entry1.subtitle: Maximum of 8 hours per day, 40 hours per week (average).Exceptions possible for up to 10 hours per day.
entity2.id4.entry2.title: Breaks
entity2.id4.entry2.subtitle: For 6-9 hours of work: 30 minute break.If over 9 hours: 45 minute break.Breaks can be shared (at least 15 minutes).
entity2.id4.entry3.title: Rest periods
entity2.id4.entry3.subtitle: Daily rest period: At least 11 hours between work shifts.Weekly rest period: At least 36 hours continuously.
entity2.id4.entry4.title: Flextime
entity2.id4.entry4.subtitle: Flexible working hours within flextime frameworks.Core time (compulsory attendance) and flexitime (free scheduling).
entity2.id5.title: Sick leave and illness
entity2.id5.subtitle: Rights in the event of illness
entity2.id5.entry1.title: Sick note
entity2.id5.entry1.subtitle: If you are sick, inform your employer immediately!See a doctor and get a certificate of incapacity for work (e-card).
entity2.id5.entry2.title: Continued payment of wages
entity2.id5.entry2.subtitle: Full continued payment of wages for 6-10 weeks depending on years of service.Then sick pay from the health insurance company (approx. 60% of salary).
entity2.id5.entry3.title: Waiting period
entity2.id5.entry3.subtitle: No waiting period in the event of an accident or occupational illness.For other illnesses: 1 day of parental leave (no pay) if the employment relationship is less than 1 month.
entity2.id5.entry4.title: Visit to the doctor during working hours
entity2.id5.entry4.subtitle: Visits to the doctor are possible during working hours.Must be announced to the employer.Time is paid as normal.
entity2.id6.title: Vacation & Leisure
entity2.id6.subtitle: Statutory vacation entitlement
entity2.id6.entry1.title: Annual leave
entity2.id6.entry1.subtitle: At least 25 working days of vacation per year (5 weeks).With a collective agreement often 30 days (6 weeks).
entity2.id6.entry2.title: Holiday pay
entity2.id6.entry2.subtitle: In addition to salary: holiday pay (1 month's salary) and Christmas bonus (1 month's salary).Mostly in June and November.
entity2.id6.entry3.title: Special leave
entity2.id6.entry3.subtitle: Paid: Wedding (1 day), death of a close relative (1-3 days), birth of a child (1 day).Unpaid: Caring for sick children.
entity2.id6.entry4.title: Parental leave
entity2.id6.entry4.subtitle: Both parents are entitled to parental leave until the child's second birthday.State childcare allowance during this time.
entity2.id7.title: Maternity protection and parental leave
entity2.id7.subtitle: Special protection rights
entity2.id7.entry1.title: Maternity leave
entity2.id7.entry1.subtitle: Employment ban 8 weeks before and 8 weeks after birth.Full continued payment of wages.Protection against dismissal during pregnancy and 4 months after birth.
entity2.id7.entry2.title: Paternity leave
entity2.id7.entry2.subtitle: Father is entitled to 1 month of paid leave upon birth (“dad month”).Must be taken within 3 months of birth.
entity2.id7.entry3.title: Parental leave
entity2.id7.entry3.subtitle: After maternity leave: Right to part-time employment until the child is 7 years old.The employer must agree, unless operational reasons speak against it.
entity2.id7.entry4.title: : childcare allowance
entity2.id7.entry4.subtitle: State benefits during maternity leave: Variants of 12-36 months.Amount depends on the option chosen and previous income.
entity2.id8.title: Trade unions and works councils
entity2.id8.subtitle: Collective advocacy
entity2.id8.entry1.title: Joining a union
entity2.id8.entry1.subtitle: Voluntarily.Contribution: approx. 1% of gross salary.Advantages: Legal advice, support for strikes, negotiation of collective agreements.
entity2.id8.entry2.title: Collective agreement
entity2.id8.entry2.subtitle: Industry-wide contract between the union and the employers' association.Sets minimum salaries, working hours, allowances.Binding for all companies in the industry.
entity2.id8.entry3.title: Works council
entity2.id8.entry3.subtitle: Can be selected in companies with 5 or more employees.Represents employee interests and has the right to co-determination in personnel matters.
entity2.id8.entry4.title: Right to strike
entity2.id8.entry4.subtitle: Basic right, but with conditions: obligation to make peace during ongoing collective agreements, strike vote required.No pay during strike.
entity2.id9.title: Termination and Termination
entity2.id9.subtitle: Termination of the employment relationship
entity2.id9.entry1.title: Notice periods
entity2.id9.entry1.subtitle: Depending on years of service: Up to 2 years: 6 weeks, 2-5 years: 2 months, 5-15 years: 3 months, 15-25 years: 4 months, over 25 years: 5 months.
entity2.id9.entry2.title: Protection against dismissal
entity2.id9.entry2.subtitle: Special protection for: pregnant women, parents on maternity leave, works council members, severely disabled people, apprentices.Socially unjustified dismissal can be challenged.
entity2.id9.entry3.title: Dismissal compensation
entity2.id9.entry3.subtitle: If terminated by the employer after more than 3 years of service: severance payment of 2 months' salary per year of service (max. 12 months).
entity2.id9.entry4.title: Termination agreement
entity2.id9.entry4.subtitle: Termination of the employment relationship by mutual agreement.Often associated with severance pay.Advantage: Immediate entitlement to unemployment benefits.
entity2.id10.title: Discrimination and bullying
entity2.id10.subtitle: Protection against discrimination
entity2.id10.entry1.title: Equal treatment
entity2.id10.entry1.subtitle: Discrimination based on gender, age, religion, origin, disability or sexual orientation is prohibited.Claims for damages possible.
entity2.id10.entry2.title: Bullying
entity2.id10.entry2.subtitle: Systematic harassment in the workplace is prohibited.Involve the works council or equal treatment attorney.Documentation of all incidents.
entity2.id10.entry3.title: Sexual harassment
entity2.id10.entry3.subtitle: Punishable!Report immediately to your superior, works council or human resources department.Employer must take action.
entity2.id10.entry4.title: Complaint points
entity2.id10.entry4.subtitle: Labor inspectorate, equal treatment attorney, chamber of labor, trade union.Free advice and support.
entity2.id11.title: Social security and taxes
entity2.id11.subtitle: Mandatory contributions from wages
entity2.id11.entry1.title: social security
entity2.id11.entry1.subtitle: 18.12% employee share, 21.13% employer share (2023).Covers health, pension, accident and unemployment insurance.
entity2.id11.entry2.title: Payroll tax
entity2.id11.entry2.subtitle: Progressive income tax: 0-11,693€: 0%, up to 19,134€: 20%, up to 32,075€: 35%, up to 62,080€: 42%, up to 93,120€: 48%, above: 50%.
entity2.id11.entry3.title: Income tax equalization
entity2.id11.entry3.subtitle: Annual tax return possible.Reimbursement of income-related expenses, commuter allowance, child allowances.Up to 5 years retroactively.
entity2.id11.entry4.title: Commuter allowance
entity2.id11.entry4.subtitle: Tax deductibility of travel expenses to work.Height depends on distance and means of transport.Up to €4,500 annually.
entity2.id12.title: unemployment
entity2.id12.subtitle: Rights if you lose your job
entity2.id12.entry1.title: Unemployment benefits
entity2.id12.entry1.subtitle: Entitlement after 52 weeks of contributions in the last 2 years.Amount: 55% of net income (max. €5,550 gross basis).Duration: 20-52 weeks.
entity2.id12.entry2.title: Emergency assistance
entity2.id12.entry2.subtitle: After unemployment benefits expire: social assistance, needs-based.Income and assets are taken into account.
entity2.id12.entry3.title: AMS reporting requirement
entity2.id12.entry3.subtitle: If you are terminated, immediately register as unemployed with the AMS (online or in person).Weekly job search reporting requirement.
entity2.id12.entry4.title: Sanctions
entity2.id12.entry4.subtitle: If job offers or measures are refused: reduction or loss of benefits.Legal remedies available to the Federal Social Security Office.
entity3.id1.title: Preparation for the job search
entity3.id1.subtitle: First steps before you apply
entity3.id1.entry1.title: Check work permit
entity3.id1.entry1.subtitle: Depending on your residence status, you will need a work permit: Asylum seekers: after 3 months for certain jobs, those entitled to asylum: unrestricted, EU citizens: unrestricted.
entity3.id1.entry2.title: Evaluate qualifications
entity3.id1.entry2.subtitle: Check whether your foreign qualifications need to be recognized in Austria.Some professions (doctors, teachers) require nostrification.
entity3.id1.entry3.title: Knowledge of German
entity3.id1.entry3.subtitle: Most jobs require knowledge of German.Level A2 for unskilled jobs, B1-B2 for skilled workers, C1 for management positions.Take advantage of free German courses.
entity3.id1.entry4.title: Career orientation
entity3.id1.entry4.subtitle: Think about which jobs fit your skills.AMS offers free career orientation tests and advice.
entity3.id2.title: Job portals - online positions
entity3.id2.subtitle: The most important job search websites
entity3.id2.entry1.title: AMS eJob Room
entity3.id2.entry1.subtitle: Official portal of the employment service: www.ams.at/ejob.Positions updated daily, personal advice available, special programs for certain groups.
entity3.id2.entry2.title: Career.at & StepStone
entity3.id2.entry2.subtitle: Large private job portals: www.karriere.at, www.stepstone.at.Many international companies, filter functions by region and industry.
entity3.id2.entry3.title: LinkedIn & XING
entity3.id2.entry3.subtitle: Professional networks: www.linkedin.com, www.xing.com.Job offers plus networking, profile as a digital business card.
entity3.id2.entry4.title: Industry-specific portals
entity3.id2.entry4.subtitle: IT: www.kununu.com, gastronomy: www.gastrojobs.at, healthcare: www.pflegejobs.at, construction: www.baujobs.at.
entity3.id3.title: Alternative job search
entity3.id3.subtitle: Ways away from the online portals
entity3.id3.entry1.title: Unsolicited application
entity3.id3.entry1.subtitle: Direct application to companies without a job advertisement.Success rate: 30-40%.Particularly successful with SMEs (small and medium-sized enterprises).
entity3.id3.entry2.title: Newspapers & print media
entity3.id3.entry2.subtitle: Traditional job advertisements: Der Standard (Friday), Kurier (Sunday), regional newspapers.Many local jobs are only advertised that way.
entity3.id3.entry3.title: Employment agencies
entity3.id3.entry3.subtitle: Private placement agencies such as Manpower, Adecco, Randstad.Free for job seekers, companies pay commission.
entity3.id3.entry4.title: Job fairs & career days
entity3.id3.entry4.subtitle: Make personal contacts: BeSt trade fair (largest education fair), career fairs at universities, industry fairs with job areas.
entity3.id4.title: Application documents - CV
entity3.id4.subtitle: How do I write an Austrian CV?
entity3.id4.entry1.title: Structure & format
entity3.id4.entry1.subtitle: Reverse chronological order (newest first).Maximum 2 pages.Professional photo (not mandatory, but common).Clean, clear formatting.
entity3.id4.entry2.title: Content
entity3.id4.entry2.subtitle: Personal data, contact, professional experience, training, language skills (with level), IT skills, hobbies (optional).No personal information such as religion, marital status.
entity3.id4.entry3.title: Europass CV
entity3.id4.entry3.subtitle: Standardized EU format: www.europass.eu.Accepted in Austria, but not preferred.Better individualize.
entity3.id4.entry4.title: Tips for migrants
entity3.id4.entry4.subtitle: Explain foreign employers and qualifications, mention nostrification, explain gaps in your CV (e.g. asylum procedure, German course).
entity3.id5.title: Application documents - cover letter
entity3.id5.subtitle: The perfect motivation letter
entity3.id5.entry1.title: structure
entity3.id5.entry1.subtitle: Maximum 1 page, 3-4 paragraphs: introduction (why this company), body (what you offer), conclusion (call for conversation).
entity3.id5.entry2.title: Individualization
entity3.id5.entry2.subtitle: Customize each cover letter individually for the company!Write the company name, job title and reference number correctly.
entity3.id5.entry3.title: Contents
entity3.id5.entry3.subtitle: Refer to the job advertisement, give concrete examples, explain motivation, highlight strengths.No standard phrases.
entity3.id5.entry4.title: Formal
entity3.id5.entry4.subtitle: Correct salutation (“Dear Ms./Mr...”), error-free German, professional email address (not: coolboy123@...), don’t forget your signature.
entity3.id6.title: Certificates and references
entity3.id6.subtitle: Which documents do I need?
entity3.id6.entry1.title: Employment references
entity3.id6.entry1.subtitle: From previous employers.If not available: confirmation of employment or contact details of references.Have foreign certificates translated.
entity3.id6.entry2.title: Training certificates
entity3.id6.entry2.subtitle: School reports, diplomas, certificates.For foreign qualifications: include a translation and, if necessary, nostrification (recognition).
entity3.id6.entry3.title: German certificates
entity3.id6.entry3.subtitle: ÖSD, Goethe certificate, TELC or other official proof.Even if not required: voluntary participation shows commitment.
entity3.id6.entry4.title: Portfolio & work samples
entity3.id6.entry4.subtitle: For creative professions: portfolio with work samples.For craftsmen: photos of projects.Online portfolio (website, LinkedIn) is recommended.
entity3.id7.title: Interview - preparation
entity3.id7.subtitle: What to do before the interview
entity3.id7.entry1.title: Company research
entity3.id7.entry1.subtitle: Inform about companies: website, social media, news.Know products/services, understand company culture.
entity3.id7.entry2.title: Prepare questions
entity3.id7.entry2.subtitle: Practice typical questions: “Tell us about yourself”, “Why do you want to come to us?”, “What are your strengths/weaknesses?”.Prepare your own questions for companies.
entity3.id7.entry3.title: Clothing & Appearance
entity3.id7.entry3.subtitle: Appropriate professional clothing (depending on the industry).Clean, well-kept, discreet.If you are unsure: it is better to be too formal than too casual.
entity3.id7.entry4.title: punctuality
entity3.id7.entry4.subtitle: Arrive at least 10 minutes early.Plan your route in advance, check your means of transport.If you are late, call immediately!
entity3.id8.title: Interview - implementation
entity3.id8.subtitle: behavior during the conversation
entity3.id8.entry1.title: First impression
entity3.id8.entry1.subtitle: Firm handshake, eye contact, smile.Introduce yourself by name.Sit upright, don't fidget.
entity3.id8.entry2.title: communication
entity3.id8.entry2.subtitle: Speak clearly, not too quietly.Answer honestly, but phrase it positively.Answer questions directly, don't digress.
entity3.id8.entry3.title: Cultural differences
entity3.id8.entry3.subtitle: In Austria: Direct communication, objectivity, punctuality, respect hierarchies.Don't be too modest - show your own achievements!
entity3.id8.entry4.title: Salary negotiation
entity3.id8.entry4.subtitle: Don't be the first to bring up the topic.If asked: have a realistic idea (check the collective agreement).Leave room for negotiation.
entity3.id9.title: AMS Services - labor market service
entity3.id9.subtitle: Free support from the state
entity3.id9.entry1.title: Register unemployed
entity3.id9.entry1.subtitle: Report to the AMS immediately after losing your job (online or in person).Apply for unemployment benefit, arrange a consultation appointment.
entity3.id9.entry2.title: Application training
entity3.id9.entry2.subtitle: Free courses: CV writing, interview practice, online application.Also available in German.
entity3.id9.entry3.title: Retraining and further training
entity3.id9.entry3.subtitle: Financing of courses, apprenticeship qualifications, studies.Especially for jobs with a shortage of staff (IT, nursing, crafts).
entity3.id9.entry4.title: Labor foundations
entity3.id9.entry4.subtitle: Project work for non-profit organizations.Paid by the AMS, serves as bridging and qualification.
entity3.id10.title: Networking & Contacts
entity3.id10.subtitle: How to use contacts for job search?
entity3.id10.entry1.title: Personal network
entity3.id10.entry1.subtitle: Inform friends, family and acquaintances that you are looking for work.Many jobs are awarded through contacts (“hidden job market”).
entity3.id10.entry2.title: Social media
entity3.id10.entry2.subtitle: Optimize your LinkedIn profile, be active, join groups.Facebook groups for jobs in the region (e.g. “Jobs in Vienna”).
entity3.id10.entry3.title: Clubs & communities
entity3.id10.entry3.subtitle: Sports clubs, religious communities, cultural associations.Make contacts here.Migrant communities often support each other.
entity3.id10.entry4.title: Mentoring programs
entity3.id10.entry4.subtitle: Programs such as “Mentoring for Migrants” and “Job Coaching for Women”.Experienced people accompany you in your job search.
entity3.id11.title: Special target groups - refugees
entity3.id11.subtitle: Job search for people entitled to asylum and asylum seekers
entity3.id11.entry1.title: Work permit
entity3.id11.entry1.subtitle: Asylum seekers: After 3 months for seasonal work, harvest help, household work.Persons entitled to asylum: Unrestricted.Always have it checked by the AMS.
entity3.id11.entry2.title: Special programs
entity3.id11.entry2.subtitle: “Work instead of social assistance”: combined wage models.“Voluntary return with a job”: support when returning to your country of origin.
entity3.id11.entry3.title: German courses & integration
entity3.id11.entry3.subtitle: Mandatory German courses (A2) for those entitled to asylum.ÖIF offers free courses.Without knowledge of German, only very limited job opportunities.
entity3.id11.entry4.title: Contact points
entity3.id11.entry4.subtitle: Caritas, Diakonie and Volkshilfe offer special job coaching for refugees.BBU advises on labor law and recognition of qualifications.
entity3.id12.title: Job search tips and mistakes to avoid
entity3.id12.subtitle: Common mistakes and how to avoid them
entity3.id12.entry1.title: Applications en masse
entity3.id12.entry1.subtitle: Don’t send 100 identical applications!It is better to have 10 individual, well-prepared applications.Quality over quantity.
entity3.id12.entry2.title: Lack of preparation
entity3.id12.entry2.subtitle: Know nothing about the company during the conversation.Always do your research beforehand!Shows interest and professionalism.
entity3.id12.entry3.title: impatience
entity3.id12.entry3.subtitle: Looking for a job in Austria takes an average of 3-6 months.Do not give up!Report regularly to the AMS and attend courses.
entity3.id12.entry4.title: Legal traps
entity3.id12.entry4.subtitle: Avoid bogus self-employment (false work contracts), illegal work, jobs below the minimum wage!Always read the contract before starting work.
entity4.id1.title: The AMS - tasks and goals
entity4.id1.subtitle: The public employment service in Austria
entity4.id1.entry1.title: What is the AMS?
entity4.id1.entry1.subtitle: The Labor Market Service (AMS) is the central public service provider for the labor market in Austria.It mediates between job seekers and companies, pays unemployment benefits and promotes qualifications.
entity4.id1.entry2.title: Legal mandate
entity4.id1.entry2.subtitle: The AMS acts on the basis of the Labor Market Promotion Act (AMFG).Its main goal is the sustainable integration of people into the labor market.
entity4.id1.entry3.title: Free services
entity4.id1.entry3.subtitle: All AMS services for job seekers are free.The AMS is financed by unemployment insurance contributions from employees and employers.
entity4.id1.entry4.title: For employers
entity4.id1.entry4.subtitle: Companies can advertise positions with the AMS free of charge, receive support for personnel searches and apply for funding (such as apprenticeship or wage subsidies).
entity4.id2.title: Registration & initial consultation
entity4.id2.subtitle: Step 1: How to register with the AMS
entity4.id2.entry1.title: When do I have to register?
entity4.id2.entry1.subtitle: Register with the AMS immediately on the first day of your unemployment so as not to lose your entitlement to benefits.Even if you are threatened with dismissal, you can register as a job seeker as a precautionary measure.
entity4.id2.entry2.title: Online registration (AMS eService)
entity4.id2.entry2.subtitle: The first registration takes place online at 'eservice.ams.at'.You need: cell phone signature or ID-Austria, social security number, CV, last pay slips and contact details.
entity4.id2.entry3.title: Personal initial consultation
entity4.id2.entry3.subtitle: After registering online, you will receive an appointment for a personal interview at your local AMS office.Bring all relevant documents (ID, confirmation of cancellation, etc.) with you.
entity4.id2.entry4.title: Responsible body
entity4.id2.entry4.subtitle: The AMS of your main residence is responsible.You can make an appointment online or via the service hotline +43 1 501 65 0.
entity4.id3.title: Unemployment benefit (ALG)
entity4.id3.subtitle: Financial support for unemployment
entity4.id3.entry1.title: Requirements
entity4.id3.entry1.subtitle: At least 52 weeks of contributions in the last 24 months before registering as unemployed.You must be available to the job market, actively search and accept placement suggestions.
entity4.id3.entry2.title: Height and duration
entity4.id3.entry2.subtitle: The Alg amounts to approx. 55% of your last net income (up to the maximum contribution basis).The benefit period is between 20 and 52 weeks, depending on your insurance history and age.
entity4.id3.entry3.title: Application
entity4.id3.entry3.subtitle: You submit the application in a personal initial interview.The payment will be made monthly in arrears to your account.
entity4.id3.entry4.title: Suspensions and cuts
entity4.id3.entry4.subtitle: In the event of unauthorized termination without an important reason or rejection of a reasonable job offer, the salary can be blocked or reduced for 4-8 weeks.
entity4.id4.title: Emergency assistance
entity4.id4.subtitle: Connection benefit after unemployment benefit
entity4.id4.entry1.title: What is emergency assistance?
entity4.id4.entry1.subtitle: Emergency assistance is a needs-based social benefit that is paid after unemployment benefits have expired if need still exists.
entity4.id4.entry2.title: Requirements
entity4.id4.entry2.subtitle: Exhausted entitlement to unemployment benefits, further unemployment, need (income and assets are taken into account) and fulfillment of all obligations to cooperate.
entity4.id4.entry3.title: Height and duration
entity4.id4.entry3.subtitle: The altitude is lower than the alg (92-95% of the alg) and is continually monitored.In contrast to Alg, it can be purchased over many years.
entity4.id4.entry4.title: Application and extension
entity4.id4.entry4.subtitle: You must apply for emergency assistance separately.The cover is checked regularly (every 3-6 months).Changes in the household must be reported immediately.
entity4.id5.title: Job search with AMS support
entity4.id5.subtitle: Active mediation and advice
entity4.id5.entry1.title: Mediation suggestions
entity4.id5.entry1.subtitle: Your AMS advisor will suggest suitable positions for you.These suggestions are binding for you as long as the position corresponds to your profession and qualifications ('reasonableness').
entity4.id5.entry2.title: AMS eJob Room
entity4.id5.entry2.subtitle: The online job exchange 'www.ams.at/ejob' with thousands of current positions.You can create your profile, apply online and activate search orders.
entity4.id5.entry3.title: Application training
entity4.id5.entry3.subtitle: Free workshops on CVs, cover letters, online applications and interviews.Improve your chances on the job market.
entity4.id5.entry4.title: Activation measures
entity4.id5.entry4.subtitle: The AMS can invite you to job interviews at companies or send you to activation measures such as assessment centers.Participation is mandatory.
entity4.id6.title: Further training and qualification
entity4.id6.subtitle: Free courses for new opportunities
entity4.id6.entry1.title: AMS course offerings
entity4.id6.entry1.subtitle: The AMS finances and organizes a wide range of courses: from German and IT courses to application training and subject-specific retraining.
entity4.id6.entry2.title: Promotion of external courses
entity4.id6.entry2.subtitle: Under certain conditions, the AMS will also cover the costs of courses with external providers (e.g. WIFI, BFI) if these are beneficial to your job opportunities.
entity4.id6.entry3.title: Retraining & apprenticeship completion
entity4.id6.entry3.subtitle: For people without a professional qualification or with outdated qualifications, the AMS supports obtaining an apprenticeship qualification or complete professional retraining.
entity4.id6.entry4.title: Application for funding
entity4.id6.entry4.subtitle: Discuss your specific further training requirements with your AMS advisor.He checks eligibility and helps with the application.
entity4.id7.title: Obligations & Sanctions
entity4.id7.subtitle: What you need to consider
entity4.id7.entry1.title: Reporting requirements & availability
entity4.id7.entry1.subtitle: You must be available for the job market (no long, unannounced absences) and log off in a timely manner during vacation or sick leave.
entity4.id7.entry2.title: Proof of application
entity4.id7.entry2.subtitle: You are obliged to actively search for a job and submit at least 2-4 applications per month.To do this, keep an application diary.
entity4.id7.entry3.title: Acceptance of reasonable work
entity4.id7.entry3.subtitle: You must accept any reasonable work.Work that corresponds to your training, is paid according to local standards and is acceptable for your health is acceptable.
entity4.id7.entry4.title: Consequences of breach of duty
entity4.id7.entry4.subtitle: Violations (e.g. rejection of a job, failure to show up for appointments) result in sanctions: reduction or complete cancellation of the cash benefit for several weeks.
entity4.id8.title: Special target groups & help
entity4.id8.subtitle: Additional offers for special needs
entity4.id8.entry1.title: Young people (AMS young people)
entity4.id8.entry1.subtitle: Special advisors for under 25s.Programs such as 'Training until 18', youth coaching and intensive support when looking for an apprenticeship.
entity4.id8.entry2.title: People over 50
entity4.id8.entry2.subtitle: The AMS offers older job seekers coaching, skills checks and programs such as 'Aktion 20,000', which provides wage subsidies for employers.
entity4.id8.entry3.title: Women & returnees
entity4.id8.entry3.subtitle: Women's advice, courses for women returning to work, support in balancing family and work and women's service centers in every federal state.
entity4.id8.entry4.title: Migrants & refugees
entity4.id8.entry4.subtitle: Advice in various languages, targeted German courses (BERUF), recognition of foreign qualifications and programs for labor market integration.
entity5.id1.title: Basics of recognition
entity5.id1.subtitle: When is official recognition necessary?
entity5.id1.entry1.title: Two types of professions
entity5.id1.entry1.subtitle: A distinction is made between regulated and non-regulated professions.For regulated professions (e.g. doctor, architect, teacher), recognition is mandatory in order to be able to practice the profession.For non-regulated professions (e.g. office clerk, IT specialist) it is usually voluntary, but important for employers.
entity5.id1.entry2.title: The benefits of recognition
entity5.id1.entry2.subtitle: Official recognition makes your qualification visible and comparable on the Austrian labor market.It increases your job chances, often enables a higher salary and is a prerequisite for starting a course of study or being admitted to certain further training courses.
entity5.id1.entry3.title: Most important principles
entity5.id1.entry3.subtitle: The Austrian recognition system follows the EU Professional Recognition Directive and the nostrification principle.It will be checked whether your foreign qualification is equivalent to an Austrian one.Complete equivalence is not always necessary;Equivalence with requirements (subsequent qualification) is often sufficient.
entity5.id1.entry4.title: Find responsible bodies
entity5.id1.entry4.subtitle: The responsible body depends on the profession or qualification.For school qualifications it is usually the education directorate of the federal state, for university qualifications it is the public universities, for regulated professions it is the respective professional association (e.g. medical association).
entity5.id2.title: Recognition of school qualifications
entity5.id2.subtitle: Middle school leaving certificate, Matura, Abitur
entity5.id2.entry1.title: Purpose of school recognition
entity5.id2.entry1.subtitle: The recognition of a foreign school qualification is usually necessary in order to start an apprenticeship in Austria, to study at a university or technical college or to gain access to certain vocational training (e.g. in the healthcare sector).
entity5.id2.entry2.title: Responsible bodies
entity5.id2.entry2.subtitle: The education directorates in the respective federal states are responsible.The desired university itself is often responsible for recognizing the general university entrance qualification (e.g. Matura, Abitur) for a course of study.
entity5.id2.entry3.title: Required documents
entity5.id2.entry3.subtitle: As a rule, you will need: The original certificate or a certified copy, an officially certified translation (by a court-certified translator) into German, proof of the length of study and subjects taken (time table), often also a school leaving certificate note.
entity5.id2.entry4.title: Possible requirements
entity5.id2.entry4.subtitle: If there are significant differences to the Austrian curriculum, supplementary examinations can be imposed in certain subjects (e.g. German, mathematics, history).If you pass this, the qualification is considered recognized.
entity5.id3.title: Recognition of university degrees (nostrification)
entity5.id3.subtitle: Bachelor, Master, Doctorate
entity5.id3.entry1.title: What is Nostrification?
entity5.id3.entry1.subtitle: Nostrification is the formal equality procedure for foreign university degrees with an Austrian degree.It confirms scientific equivalence and entitles you to hold the corresponding academic degree (e.g. 'Master of Science, M.Sc.').
entity5.id3.entry2.title: Responsible universities
entity5.id3.entry2.subtitle: Nostrification is always carried out by an Austrian public university that offers a comparable range of courses.A mechanical engineering bachelor's degree is examined by the TU Vienna, for example.The website www.ancognition.at helps you find the responsible body.
entity5.id3.entry3.title: Documents & Translations
entity5.id3.entry3.subtitle: The following are necessary: ​​diploma/certificate (certified), diploma supplement or detailed module descriptions, CV, passport.All documents must be officially certified and translated into German.An apostille or legalization is often required.
entity5.id3.entry4.title: Test procedures & requirements
entity5.id3.entry4.subtitle: The university checks the content, scope and duration of the course of study.In the event of deviations, it may require nostrification examinations (in certain subjects) or the completion of a master's thesis.If there are larger differences, only partial nostrification is pronounced.
entity5.id4.title: Recognition in regulated professions
entity5.id4.subtitle: Doctors, engineers, teachers, nurses
entity5.id4.entry1.title: What are regulated professions?
entity5.id4.entry1.subtitle: These are professions whose practice is legally linked to the possession of a specific qualification in order to protect public health or safety.Full recognition (“professional authorization”) is a legal obligation here.Examples: doctor, pharmacist, architect, psychologist, teacher, electrical engineer.
entity5.id4.entry2.title: Responsible chambers & authorities
entity5.id4.entry2.subtitle: Each profession has its own responsible chamber or authority: for health professions the respective state medical or health professional chamber, for engineers the Chamber of Engineers, for teachers the Federal Ministry of Education.A list of all positions can be found at www.berufsanwissen.at.
entity5.id4.entry3.title: Special procedure
entity5.id4.entry3.subtitle: In addition to the examination of qualifications, a knowledge test or an adaptation course (internship under supervision) is often required.For EU/EEA citizens, an accelerated procedure applies according to the EU Professional Recognition Directive.The procedure is often more complex for third-country nationals.
entity5.id4.entry4.title: Language certificate
entity5.id4.entry4.subtitle: For almost all regulated professions, proof of German language skills at level B2 or C1 (GER) is mandatory before submitting an application.For example, ÖSD, Goethe or telc certificates are recognized.
entity5.id5.title: Assessment of non-regulated professions & professional experience
entity5.id5.subtitle: Apprenticeship qualifications, training, informal learning
entity5.id5.entry1.title: Voluntary assessment
entity5.id5.entry1.subtitle: There is no requirement for recognition for non-regulated professions (e.g. chef, retail clerk, software developer).However, it makes sense to have your qualifications formally assessed by the Chamber of Commerce (WKO) or the AMS in order to make them understandable for employers.
entity5.id5.entry2.title: Recognition of professional experience
entity5.id5.entry2.subtitle: Competencies acquired informally (through many years of professional experience) can also be recognized!The process is called “Validation of non-formal and informally acquired skills”.It often ends with a formal certificate (e.g. an “AMS certificate of competence”).
entity5.id5.entry3.title: Competency assessment
entity5.id5.entry3.subtitle: In an assessment process (discussions, practical exercises, work samples) your skills are analyzed and compared with an Austrian professional profile.This can be done at the AMS, in career information centers (BIZ) or at specialized institutions such as abif.
entity5.id5.entry4.title: Result and benefit
entity5.id5.entry4.subtitle: You will receive an official report or certificate that certifies your skills.You can enclose this document with applications.It can also show what missing qualifications you need to catch up on in order to obtain a formal qualification.
entity5.id6.title: Practical process, costs and duration
entity5.id6.subtitle: What to expect
entity5.id6.entry1.title: Step-by-step process
entity5.id6.entry1.subtitle:
1. Get advice (e.g. from AST).
2. Determine the responsible body.
3. Collect documents, have them certified and translated.
4. Submit the application with all documents.
5. Complete procedures and any exams/requirements.
6. Notification (certificate of recognition) received.
entity5.id6.entry2.title: Costs & Fees
entity5.id6.entry2.subtitle: The costs vary greatly: certifications and translations (€50-150 per document), administrative fees from the recognition office (€100-600), costs for supplementary examinations or courses (can amount to several thousand euros).There are often options for covering costs for those entitled to asylum and those entitled to subsidiary protection.
entity5.id6.entry3.title: Duration of the procedure
entity5.id6.entry3.subtitle: The duration depends on the completeness of your documents and the type of procedure: School qualifications: 1-3 months.Nostrification: 3-9 months.Regulated professions (EU): up to 4 months.Regulated professions (third country): 6 months to several years.Plan enough time!
entity5.id6.entry4.title: Legal remedies
entity5.id6.entry4.subtitle: You can lodge a complaint against a negative decision or disproportionate requirements within 4 weeks.Be sure to seek support from a legal advice center (e.g. the Chamber of Labor or a migrant advice center).
entity5.id7.title: Support and advice
entity5.id7.subtitle: Get free help
entity5.id7.entry1.title: Recognition Contact Point (AST)
entity5.id7.entry1.subtitle: The “Recognition Contact Point” is the federal government’s central, free advice center.It helps you find the responsible office, explains the procedure and supports you in compiling documents.Contact: Telephone +43 1 531 20 0, Email: ancognition@bmbwf.gv.at.
entity5.id7.entry2.title: Migration advice centers
entity5.id7.entry2.subtitle: Organizations such as Caritas, Diakonie, Volkshilfe and migrant advice centers offer special advice on recognition issues for people with a migrant background, often in several languages.
entity5.id7.entry3.title: AMS & career information centers (BIZ)
entity5.id7.entry3.subtitle: The AMS advises on professional recognition as part of work integration and can provide funding for recognition procedures or necessary subsequent qualifications.You can find out about professional profiles in the BIS.
entity5.id7.entry4.title: Funding opportunities
entity5.id7.entry4.subtitle: Under certain conditions, the AMS, the ÖIF (Austrian Integration Fund) or funds such as MYKI (Migrant Competence) cover parts of the costs for translations, fees or required courses.Ask your advice center about it!
entity5.id8.title: Alternatives to full recognition
entity5.id8.subtitle: If nostrification is not possible (immediately).
entity5.id8.entry1.title: Post-qualification & additional training
entity5.id8.entry1.subtitle: If your qualification is not fully recognized, you can catch up on the missing skills.The AMS often supports courses, internships or retaking partial exams in order to achieve recognition.
entity5.id8.entry2.title: Working in auxiliary positions
entity5.id8.entry2.subtitle: In some regulated professions (e.g. nursing, technology) it is possible to initially work as an assistant or assistant while you prepare for full recognition in parallel.This provides practical experience and an income.
entity5.id8.entry3.title: Recognition of partial competencies
entity5.id8.entry3.subtitle: Even if the entire qualification is not recognized, individual subjects or modules can be credited - for example when studying later in Austria.Have a detailed report issued that shows these partial equivalences.
entity5.id8.entry4.title: Competency-oriented application
entity5.id8.entry4.subtitle: In your application, focus on your specific skills and professional experience, not just on the formal title.A professional skills profile or letters of reference from previous employers can partially compensate for the lack of an Austrian qualification.
entity6.id1.title: Dual apprenticeship - the Austrian model of success
entity6.id1.subtitle: Practice in the company and theory in the vocational school
entity6.id1.entry1.title: What is a doctrine?
entity6.id1.entry1.subtitle: Dual training is the most common training model in Austria.As an apprentice, you work 3-4 days per week in a company and attend vocational school for 1-2 days.The training lasts 2-4 years and ends with the final apprenticeship examination (LAP).
entity6.id1.entry2.title: Advantages of teaching
entity6.id1.entry2.subtitle: You earn money right from the start (apprenticeship compensation), gain practical experience and have very good job opportunities after graduation.There are over 200 apprenticeships to choose from, from electrical engineering to retail to information technology.
entity6.id1.entry3.title: Requirements
entity6.id1.entry3.subtitle: The minimum requirement is usually completion of the 9th grade (compulsory school).For some professions, a positive completion of the 8th or 9th grade in certain subjects is required.The minimum age is 15 years.
entity6.id1.entry4.title: Apprenticeship search
entity6.id1.entry4.subtitle: You can find apprenticeships in the AMS eJob Room, at the WKO apprenticeship office, directly at companies or at trade fairs such as BeSt³.An unsolicited application to companies that are not explicitly looking is very successful.
entity6.id2.title: Vocational schools (BMS/BHS)
entity6.id2.subtitle: Full-time schools for higher qualifications
entity6.id2.entry1.title: Vocational middle school (BMS)
entity6.id2.entry1.subtitle: Duration: 1-4 years.Degree: Skilled worker certificate or final examination.BMS prepare you for a specific profession (e.g. nursing assistant, electrical engineering, office).Some complete with a final apprenticeship examination.
entity6.id2.entry2.title: Vocational secondary school (BHS)
entity6.id2.entry2.subtitle: Duration: 5 years.Qualification: Matriculation and diploma examination (Matura + professional qualification).A BHS (such as HTL, HAK, HLW) offers full vocational training and general university entrance qualifications.Very good job prospects!
entity6.id2.entry3.title: Admission requirements
entity6.id2.entry3.subtitle: For BMS: Positive completion of the 8th grade.For BHS: Positive completion of the 8th grade, often with entrance exams in German, mathematics and English.If demand is excessive, there is an admission process.
entity6.id2.entry4.title: Costs and financing
entity6.id2.entry4.subtitle: Public vocational schools are free.Material costs (workshop, cooking clothing) may apply.There are special evening schools or colleges for adults (2 years after graduation).
entity6.id3.title: Adult education courses
entity6.id3.subtitle: Further training alongside your job
entity6.id3.entry1.title: WiFi and BFI
entity6.id3.entry1.subtitle: The Economic Development Institutes (WiFi) of the Chamber of Commerce and the Vocational Development Institutes (BFI) offer thousands of courses: from crafts and technology to office and management to languages ​​and IT.Qualifications: certificates, diplomas, master's examination.
entity6.id3.entry2.title: Adult education centers (VHS)
entity6.id3.entry2.subtitle: The adult education centers offer a wide range of inexpensive courses for all interests: languages, health, creativity, basic education and key professional skills (e.g. IT, application training).
entity6.id3.entry3.title: Educational centers & academies
entity6.id3.entry3.subtitle: Private and denominational education providers (e.g. Catholic Education Center, state education centers) offer seminars and longer-term training, often with a focus on social, educational or personality-building topics.
entity6.id3.entry4.title: Online learning platforms
entity6.id3.entry4.subtitle: MOOC platforms (such as iMoox.at), the ÖIF learning platform (sprachportal.at) or courses on Udemy and Coursera enable flexible learning.You will often receive certificates of participation, which are valuable on your CV.
entity6.id4.title: Obtain formal qualifications
entity6.id4.subtitle: Compulsory school leaving certificate, high school diploma and university entrance qualification
entity6.id4.entry1.title: Completion of compulsory schooling
entity6.id4.entry1.subtitle: Anyone who has completed 9 years of compulsory schooling without a positive result can do so free of charge.Offers are available from the BFI, VHS and other providers.Often in modular form, also possible part-time.
entity6.id4.entry2.title: Vocational maturity test (BRP)
entity6.id4.entry2.subtitle: The BRP is the full-fledged Matura replacement for people with an apprenticeship qualification or professional experience.It consists of 4 partial exams (German, mathematics, living foreign language, subject area) and entitles you to study at universities, technical colleges and colleges.
entity6.id4.entry3.title: Study entrance qualification test (SBP)
entity6.id4.entry3.subtitle: The SBP entitles you to study a specific subject at universities and technical colleges without having to hold a high school diploma.It is put together individually and consists of several exams that cover the required prior knowledge.
entity6.id4.entry4.title: Preparatory courses
entity6.id4.entry4.subtitle: WiFi, BFI, VHS and private providers offer preparation courses for BRP and SBP.The courses can be funded (e.g. by AMS, the Chamber of Labor or the WAFF in Vienna).
entity6.id5.title: AMS-funded training and further education
entity6.id5.subtitle: Free qualification for job seekers
entity6.id5.entry1.title: German courses
entity6.id5.entry1.subtitle: The AMS finances German courses from A1 to C1, especially the BERUF German courses, which teach job-related German.A1 and A2 courses are often mandatory for those entitled to asylum and those entitled to subsidiary protection.
entity6.id5.entry2.title: Application training & skills training
entity6.id5.entry2.subtitle: Free courses on CV, online application, interview and self-presentation.Courses on basic digital skills or project management are also offered.
entity6.id5.entry3.title: Retraining and specialist training
entity6.id5.entry3.subtitle: The AMS finances complete retraining in shortage occupations (e.g. nursing, IT, electrical engineering, warehouse logistics).Training takes place at educational institutions, often including internships.You will receive support money during your training.
entity6.id5.entry4.title: Apprenticeship qualification for adults
entity6.id5.entry4.subtitle: Through the “Apprenticeship with Matura” program or the “Complete Apprenticeship Examination for Adults” adults can obtain an apprenticeship qualification in a shorter period of time (1-2 years).The AMS covers course costs and offers financial support.
entity6.id6.title: Industry-specific training
entity6.id6.subtitle: Special paths into sought-after professions
entity6.id6.entry1.title: Nursing and health professions
entity6.id6.entry1.subtitle: Training as a nursing assistant (2 years) or qualified health and nursing (3 years, FH degree).Schools: Health and nursing schools at hospitals, technical colleges.Great need for skilled workers!
entity6.id6.entry2.title: IT & digitalization
entity6.id6.entry2.subtitle: Training paths: Apprenticeship (app development, information technology), HTL (Higher Technical College), FH studies or certificate courses (e.g. at WIFI for coding, network technology, cybersecurity).
entity6.id6.entry3.title: Construction and skilled trades
entity6.id6.entry3.subtitle: The classic route is apprenticeship (bricklayer, carpenter, plumber).Advancement through master's examination (preparation at WIFI).HTL for construction technology or college for construction management are also possible.
entity6.id6.entry4.title: Gastronomy & Tourism
entity6.id6.entry4.subtitle: Apprenticeship (cook, restaurant specialist), hotel management school (intermediate school), tourism schools (higher schools) or technical college courses.Short training courses for baristas or sommeliers are also popular.
entity6.id7.title: Financing and grants
entity6.id7.subtitle: Support with costs
entity6.id7.entry1.title: AMS funding
entity6.id7.entry1.subtitle: The AMS can cover 100% of the course costs if the further training increases job opportunities.During longer full-time courses, they pay support allowance (similar to unemployment benefit).
entity6.id7.entry2.title: Educational leave and part-time educational work
entity6.id7.entry2.subtitle: Educational leave: Up to 1 year of paid leave from work for further training.Part-time educational work: Reduction of working hours to 25-75% for up to 4 years with simultaneous training.In both cases you will receive further training money from the AMS.
entity6.id7.entry3.title: Funding from states and foundations
entity6.id7.entry3.subtitle: Federal states have their own funds (e.g. WAFF in Vienna, SFG in Styria).Foundations such as the Chamber of Labor (AK) for Education Support or the Talented Support Fund provide support with costs.
entity6.id7.entry4.title: Tax deductibility
entity6.id7.entry4.subtitle: Costs for training and further education that are related to your job can be claimed as business expenses in the employee assessment (wage tax compensation).That saves taxes.
entity6.id8.title: Competency recording & recognition
entity6.id8.subtitle: Make the most of your prior knowledge
entity6.id8.entry1.title: Competence balance & potential analysis
entity6.id8.entry1.subtitle: The AMS or BIZ (vocational information centers) offer free potential analyzes.Strengths, interests and possible career paths are identified in discussions and tests.This helps you choose the right training.
entity6.id8.entry2.title: Validation of informally acquired skills
entity6.id8.entry2.subtitle: Work experience but no degree?You can have your skills tested and certified through a validation process (e.g. at the BFI or abif).This can lead to a partial or complete apprenticeship completion.
entity6.id8.entry3.title: Credit for training
entity6.id8.entry3.subtitle: Previous knowledge from previous training or abroad can often be credited towards a new training course.This shortens the duration of training.Speak to the training institution or the WKO apprenticeship office.
entity6.id8.entry4.title: Educational advice Austria
entity6.id8.entry4.subtitle: The Educational Advice Network Austria offers free, neutral and confidential advice on all educational paths.By telephone, online or in person at one of the many advice centers in all federal states.
